part1.title: The Creator: Ultimate Ground, Origin, and Cause
part1.label: Part opening
part1.summary: Creation cannot explain its own existence. It points beyond itself to the Creator as the first cause and ground of being.
part1.imageAlt: Cosmic and natural landscape representing the Creator as the ground and origin of existence

p1-1.title: Creator and Creation: A Relationship of Fulfillment
p1-1.summary: The Creator's fullness overflows into creation. Creation, in turn, finds meaning through relationship with its source.
p1-1.imageAlt: An abundant natural spring flowing into a flourishing landscape

p1-2.title: The Yearning for Oneness
p1-2.summary: All things come from one source and yearn for reunion. The Creator reaches outward as creation turns inward.
p1-2.imageAlt: A lone person in prayer overlooking a vast mountain valley at sunrise

p1-3.title: Visible and Invisible: Two Expressions of Creation
p1-3.summary: Visible matter and invisible order belong together. One gives the other a place to be expressed.
p1-3.imageAlt: A flowering tree in a harmonious natural landscape

p1-4.title: The Creator Known Through Creation
p1-4.summary: The Creator exceeds our full understanding, yet is not absent. Creation bears traces of divine intelligence, beauty, goodness, and order.
p1-4.imageAlt: Scholars studying the night sky through a telescope

part2.title: Humanity: Heaven’s Breath in Earthly Clay
part2.label: Part opening
part2.summary: Humanity unites the visible body and invisible soul in one living being. Through embodied action, spirit and will take form in the world.
part2.imageAlt: Adam in the Garden of Eden surrounded by living creation

p2-1.title: The Gift of Likeness
p2-1.summary: The human soul seeks meaning, purpose, truth, and freedom. We flourish as we reflect the Creator's nurturing goodness in our lives.
p2-1.imageAlt: A thoughtful person considering meaning, moral values, and a higher calling

p2-2.title: Relationship and Oneness: Humanity’s Twin Yearnings
p2-2.summary: We seek relationship with the Creator and oneness with one another. Love expands from the self and family to all humanity.
p2-2.imageAlt: A family embracing beneath a starry night sky

p2-3.title: Soul and Body: A Life on Mission
p2-3.summary: The soul gives life its direction; the body makes action possible. A meaningful life joins both in service of a calling.
p2-3.imageAlt: A busy office worker reflecting on his life purpose

p2-4.title: Free Will and Intelligence: Gifts and Responsibilities
p2-4.summary: Free will gives us the power to choose. Intelligence helps us learn from consequences and grow in wisdom.
p2-4.imageAlt: A person at a crossroads between peace and destruction

p2-5.title: Demands and Rewards: Existence with Purpose
p2-5.summary: Life brings real needs and real pleasures, but neither is its ultimate purpose. Our calling should guide how we work and enjoy.
p2-5.imageAlt: A family working together in a garden and enjoying the rewards of their work

p2-6.title: Divine Ownership and Human Possession
p2-6.summary: The Creator holds ultimate ownership, while human possession remains a real right. Stewardship calls us to care for and share what we hold.
p2-6.imageAlt: A farmer sharing the harvest with a neighboring family

p2-7.title: Hardship, Suffering, and Greater Understanding
p2-7.summary: Hardship can reveal what we do not yet understand. Recording and sharing those lessons helps prevent harm from recurring.
p2-7.imageAlt: Flood survivors, a scholar recording lessons, and children reading in a library
